(72) One should cook six-ingredient ghee in the fresh juice of āmalaka fruits.
Combined with sugar and rock salt, that is beneficial for all those suffering from abdominal tumors (gulma).
[This oil] is cooked with a paste consisting of six palas each of Pippalī, Pippalīmūla, Cavya, Viśvauṣadha, Citraka, and Yavakṣāra.
One *prastha* of ghee, boiled with a decoction of *daśamūla*, *urubūka*, and *bhārgī*, along with milk and curd, is known as the "Six-Pala" (*ṣaṭpala*) formulation;
it cures abdominal tumors (*gulma*), abdominal enlargement (*udara*), anorexia, fistula-in-ano (*bhagaṇḍara*), and impaired digestion (*vahnisāda*). (74)

Experts declare this "Six-Pala Preparation of Bhārgī" to immediately pacify cough, fever, consumption, stiffness of the head, disorders of the digestive tract (grahaṇī), and those ailments arising from phlegm and wind. (75)
One should cook one *prastha* of ghee with one *pala* each of pippalī, pippalīmūla, cavya, citraka, and nāgara,
along with barley alkali (*yavakṣāra*) and one *prastha* of milk; that ghee destroys *gulma* caused by *kapha*.
It destroys malabsorption (grahaṇī) and anemia (pāṇḍuroga), and removes splenic enlargement, cough, and fever. 77.
Two palas of bhallātaka and one pala each of the five roots (pañcamūla), enriched with vidārīgandhā and the rest, should be boiled in an āḍhaka of water from the āpotttha plant. 78.
When the decoction is strained and reduced to one-quarter, the physician should grind together one karṣa each of pippalī, nāgara, vacā,
viḍaṅga, saindhava, hiṅgu, yāvaśūka, biḍa, śaṭhī,
citraka, madhuka, and rāsnā.
Having added one prastha of milk, one should cook one prastha of ghee;
this preparation, known as Bhallātaka, is supreme for removing Kapha-type Gulma, and it cures splenic disorders, anemia, asthma, malabsorption syndrome (Grahani), cough, and abdominal tumors.
Clarified butter should be prepared with the juice of garlic, combined with the decoction of the five roots (pañcamūla),
along with the juices of wine, fermented rice-water, sour curd, and radish,
together with trikaṭu, pomegranate, wood-apple, yamānī, cavya, and rock salt.

A preparation cooked with one pala each of hiṅgu, amlavetasa, ajājī, and dīpyaka conquers abdominal tumors (gulma), malabsorption syndrome (grahaṇī), hemorrhoids (arśas), asthma, insanity, consumption,
fever, cough, epilepsy, weak digestion, splenic enlargement, colic, and disorders of vāta.
Twenty-five *abhayā* fruits, as many *palas* of *dantī*, and the same amount of *citraka* should be boiled in one *droṇa* of water.
When reduced to one-eighth, one should cook an equal amount of jaggery (*guḍa*) with that decoction.
From those [drugs], four palas each of the powder of abhayā and trivṛt, and also from oil;
one pala each of pippalī and śuṇṭhī; and when the linctus is prepared and cooled, one should add honey equal to the oil, as well as one pala of the cāturjātaka.
Then, having licked one pala of the electuary and eaten one *harītakī*, the person— being oleated— is easily purged of a prastha of morbid humors (*doṣa*) and becomes free from disease.
[It cures] splenic disorders, edema, abdominal tumors, hemorrhoids, heart disease, anemia, and diseases of the *grahaṇī*.
Indigestion, distressing fevers, leprosy, and loss of appetite are pacified. 89.
One should boil vṛścīra, urubūka, varṣābhū, the two types of bṛhatī, and citraka in one droṇa of water until it is reduced to one-fourth. 90.
One should place it in a jar smeared with Māgadhī, Citraka, and honey, having added one *prastha* of honey and combined it with half a *karṣa* of powdered *pathyā*.
After letting it sit for ten days, a person who has finished his meal should drink it at dawn.
This Ariṣṭa shall conquer Gulma and the very difficult-to-cure Avipāka.

However, in the case of a blood-born (raudhira) Gulma when the time for delivery has passed, one should administer an unctuous purgative to a patient whose body has been treated with oleation and sudation.
A paste made from *śatāhvā*, the bark of *cirabilva*, *dāru*, *bhārgī*, and *kaṇā*, when drunk with a decoction of sesame, removes *gulma* born of blood.
A decoction of sesame, combined with jaggery, the three pungents (*vyoṣa*), asafoetida (*hiṅgu*), and *bhārgī*, should be used [in this manner].

For women suffering from blood-born gulma and loss of menses, one should drink wine mixed with alkali and the three pungents (tryūṣaṇa). Furthermore, she who suffers from blood-gulma should drink ghee prepared with the alkaline water of *palāśa*. || 95-96 ||
One should cause it to break open with hot [applications]; once it has broken, the regimen for menorrhagia (asṛgdara) is beneficial.

If it does not break open even thus, one should administer a vaginal cleanser (yoni-śodhana) consisting of minced meat (palala) mixed with alkali (kṣāra) or with the milky sap of the Sudhā plant. || 97 ||
If the bleeding is excessive, however, one should employ treatments that alleviate *raktapitta* (hemorrhagic disorders).
One should drink ghee prepared with the paste and decoction of *bhallātaka*, mixed with sugar.

When drunk with honey, it destroys that blood-bile (raktapitta) as well as phlegm-induced abdominal tumors (balāsagulma). [One should avoid] dried meat, radish, fish, and dried vegetables which cause pain.
One suffering from abdominal tumors (gulma) should not eat yams or sweet fruits. When the heart is afflicted by vāta, one should cause the patient to vomit after first administering oleation.
With a decoction of the two groups of five roots (dvipañcamūlī) mixed with oil and salt,
one should sprinkle [the patient] with a powder of long pepper, cardamom, vacā, asafoetida, alkali of barley, rock salt, black salt, ginger, and ajamodā.
One whose body has been purified should be made to drink fruit-acid, sour gruel, horse gram, curd, wine, or fermented liquors, or any one of these along with an unctuous substance.
Alternatively, one should drink warm *jāgara* or a decoction that increases the digestive fire.
It alleviates cough, dyspnea, and wind disorders, and destroys colic and heart disease.

When the heart is afflicted by pitta, one should induce vomiting with water mixed with śrīparṇī, madhuka, honey, sugar, and jaggery; furthermore, one should consume [medicines] boiled with sweet substances.
Ghee and the decoctions specified as destroyers of pitta-fever [should be used]; likewise,
cold plasters, affusions,
and purgation are indicated when the heart is afflicted by pitta.
With grapes, sugar, honey, and *parūṣaka*, there should be food and drink that pacifies *pitta* once [the system] is purified;
or one may drink [a paste] made by grinding these with sugar-water.
One should employ milk prepared with yaṣṭyāhvaya, tiktakarohiṇī,
and the bark of arjuna for heart disease,
either with sugar, or with the five roots (pañcamūlī), or with balā, or with madhuka. || 8–9 ||
Those who drink the powder of *kakubha* bark with ghee, milk, or jaggery-water overcome heart disease,
chronic fever, and hemorrhagic disorders (*raktapitta*).
Having killed [the worms], they would become long-lived.
When phlegm arises in the heart, one should administer an emetic using a decoction of *vacā* and *nimba*, and apply the *pippalyādi* powder which removes heart disease caused by *vāta*.
In cases arising from the three doṣas, fasting should be administered first; furthermore, food that is beneficial for all [three types] should be prescribed,
having considered whether the condition is mild, moderate, or severe.
The medicinal action of all three is likewise praised.
One should lick lotus-pollen mixed with honey;
it destroys heart-ache, cough, and asthma, and wards off consumption and hiccup.
Or he who drinks a continuous dose of wheat or barley flour cooked with oil, clarified butter, and molasses.

A person becomes one who has conquered all heart-disease by consuming wheat and *kakubha* flour cooked in goat’s milk, cow’s ghee, and fresh butter. || 14 || [The powder of wheat and *kakubha* is cooked in goat’s milk, cow’s ghee, and fresh butter.]
Combined with honey and sugar,
it pacifies severe heart disease in men.
One should cause the powder of the root of Nāgabalā to be drunk with milk.
The bark of the *kakubha* tree destroys heart disease, asthma, and cough.
When combined with meat, it is a supreme elixir (*rasāyana*), strengthening and subduing wind (*vāta*).
By its use for one year, one may live for two hundred years.
One should drink asafoetida, ugragandhā, biḍa salt, viśva, kṛṣṇā, kuṣṭha, abhayā, citraka, yavaśūka, along with sauvarcala salt and puṣkaramūla.
Barley water [is used] for heart disease and ailments of the abdomen.
A decoction of the ten roots (daśamūlī), combined with salt and alkali,
destroys cough, dyspnea, heart disease, abdominal tumors (gulma), and colic pain.
One pala each of pāṭhā, vacā, yavakṣāra, abhayā, amlavetasa, durālabhā, citraka, tryūṣaṇa, śaṭhī,
puṣkaramūla, tintiḍīka, and pomegranate [should be taken]. || 20 ||
One should have the roots of the mātuluṅga made into a fine powder.
One should have this powder drunk with lukewarm water or with wines;
it quickly dispels hemorrhoids, colic, heart disease, and abdominal tumors.
For one who drinks deer horn that has been burnt in a closed crucible and ground with stone along with clarified butter,
the pain in the heart and back is pacified.
Even a difficult condition soon comes to an end.

One should feed a patient suffering from heart disease caused by worms with unctuous rice and meat, along with curd and minced meat, for three days; thereafter, one should administer a purgative. || 23-24 ||
One should cause [the patient] to drink fermented grain-water (dhānyāmla) mixed with fragrant substances, salt, cumin, sugar, and a large quantity of viḍaṅga; this is most beneficial.
In cases of worms, one should also drink urine combined with viḍaṅga and iron.
Thus, worms residing in the heart of men fall downward; thereafter,
one should give him barley-food along with viḍaṅga and fifty of the best harītakīs.
Two palas of sauvarcala salt and ghee cooked together is known by the name Vallabhaka;
it destroys heart-disease, dyspnea, colic, abdominal ailments, and wind disorders. (27)
One should cook one *pala* each of *aśvadaṃṣṭrā*, *uśīra*, *mañjiṣṭhā*, *balā*, *kāśmarya*, *kattṛṇa*,
the root of *darbha*, *pṛthakparṇī*, *palāśa*, *ṛṣabhaka*, and *sthirā*; then,
[add] four times as much milk to their decoction.
A *prastha* of ghee prepared with the pastes of *svaguptā*, *ṛṣabhaka*, goat’s marrow, *jīvantī*,
the two types of *jīraka*, *śatāvarī*, *ṛddhi*, *mṛdvīkā*, sugar, *śrāvaṇī*, and *viṣa* cures diseases of the heart caused by *vāta* and *pitta*, as well as colic. (29–30)
This ghee, prepared with the decoction of *balā*, *nāgabalā*, and *arjuna*, cures dysuria, urinary disorders (*prameha*), hemorrhoids, asthma, cough, and consumption;
it bestows strength and muscle upon those emaciated by archery, women, wine, heavy loads, or long journeys.
(31) 7. Ghee [prepared with] the water of *balā*, *nāgabalā*, and *arjuna*.
This proven formulation, containing a quarter-part of a paste of yaṣṭīmadhu,
pacifies severe heart disease, pain from ulcers, hemorrhaging, cough, and disorders of wind and blood. || 32 ||
Ghee prepared with the juice of the paste of pārtha is recommended for all heart diseases.
(33) Chapter 31.
One should administer oil massages, oleation, non-unctuous enemas, sudation, poultices, urethral/vaginal enemas,
and affusions prepared with the *sthirā* group and other Vata-alleviating herbs.

One should administer juices in cases of wind-related dysuria. Afflicted by diseases of Vata, accompanied by pain and dysuria, one should drink a decoction of Amṛtā, Nāgara, Dhātrī, Vājigandhā, and Trikaṇṭaka.
Immersion baths, cooling plasters, the summer regimen, enemas, preparations of milk, and treatments with grape juice, vidārī root juice, sugarcane juice, and ghee [are recommended].
In difficult conditions arising from pitta, these should be employed:
Kuśa, Kāśa, Śara, Darbha, and Ikṣu; this group of five roots (pañcamūla) derived from grasses removes pitta-induced dysuria and cleanses the bladder.
This unctuous milk, when drunk, destroys blood located in the penis.
[It is prepared from] śatāvarī, kāśa, kuśa, śvadaṃṣṭrā, vidārī, śālī, ikṣu, and kaśeruka.
Drinking a well-cooled decoction mixed with honey and sugar cures urinary distress caused by pitta (paittika-mūtrakṛcchra).
[A decoction of] harītakī, gokṣura, and rājavṛkṣa...
One should drink a decoction of pāṣāṇabhida, dhanvana, and vāsaka, combined with honey,
in cases of painful dysuria accompanied by burning, pain, and constipation.
Amalaka with jaggery is aphrodisiac, destroys fatigue, and is supremely satiating;
it alleviates pitta, blood disorders, burning sensations, and colic, and prevents dysuria.
(7) Ervāru seeds, madhuka, and aravinda—along with dārvī—[are beneficial].
In cases of urinary distress caused by pitta, one should drink dārvī with rice-washings, or likewise āmalakī juice mixed with honey, for the pitta-type mūtrakṛcchra.
Alkaline, hot, sharp, and pungent food and drink; sudation; barley-based diet; emesis; non-unctuous enemas (nirūha); buttermilk; and oil prepared with bitter medicinal herbs.
Anointing, massage, and drinking [of these] are for [the treatment of] phlegm and dysuria.
For the destruction of phlegm-induced dysuria, one should drink Truṭi ground finely with urine, wine, or the fresh juice of the plantain (kadalī).
One should drink the seeds of *śitimāraka* mixed with buttermilk for the purpose of destroying urinary distress (*kṛcchra*);
likewise, one should drink them with rice-wash water.

Coral powder [is used] for phlegm and dysuria (kapha-mūtrakṛcchra). Alternatively, *śvadaṃṣṭrā* with water or *viśva* with water destroys phlegm-induced dysuria. However, in the case of dysuria arising from all three *doṣas*, it is for the wind (*vāyu*).

Having carefully considered the sequence of the bodily sites, the treatment should be applied; when [the doshas] exceed three, emesis should first be administered for kapha, purgation for pitta, and enema for vāta. (13)
The *bṛhatyādi* group— consisting of *bṛhatī*, *dhāvanī*, *pāṭhā*, *yaṣṭīmadhuka*, and *liṅgaka*— is digestive (*pācanīya*) and removes the three doṣas associated with urinary disorders (*kṛcchra*).
Likewise, in cases arising from trauma (*abhighātaja*), one should immediately apply the treatment for wounds.
In cases of dysuria (mūtrakṛcchra), Vāta-alleviating treatment should always be administered.
When caused by feces (purīṣaja), sudation, powder therapy, massage, and enemas should be employed;
one should drink a decoction of Gokṣura seeds combined with Yava-kṣāra. || 15–16 ||
When drunk, it quickly cures dysuria and that which is born from feces. The therapeutic measures beneficial for dysuria caused by kapha and vāta are also beneficial for urinary calculi and gravel.

In cases arising from the obstruction of semen, one should consume a linctus of *śilājatu* mixed with honey; furthermore, women of excellent qualities should be enjoyed by one whose bodily tissues have been nourished by aphrodisiacs (*vṛṣya*).
A man should drink milk combined with cardamom (*elā*) and asafoetida (*hiṅgu*), mixed with clarified butter (*sarpiḥ*).
It serves to purify defects of the urine and removes defects of the semen.
Whatever has been prescribed for dysuria caused by Pitta should also be administered in dysuria caused by blood.
Trikaṇṭaka, āragvadha, darbha, kāśa, durālabhā, parvatabheda,
and pathyā, when drunk with honey, destroy urinary calculi.
Even for one whose death has arrived, dysuria [is cured];
a decoction prepared with the root of atibalā conquers all forms of dysuria.
[A compound] of elā, aśmabheda, śilājatu, and pippalī...
Having drunk these powders stirred with rice-water, or having licked them mixed with jaggery,
even one who is near death from dysuria shall live.
Iron powder, finely ground and mixed with honey,
when taken in three linctuses, undoubtedly destroys dysuria quickly.
Equal parts of sugar and barley-alkali (yavakṣāra) are a remedy that wards off all types of dysuria.
Or the juice of *nidigdhikā* mixed with honey is a destroyer of urinary distress (*kṛcchra*).
[The water] boiled with *śatāvarī*, *kāśa*, *kuśa*, *śvadaṃṣṭrā*, *vidārī*, sugarcane, and *āmalaka* is likewise effective.
Ghee or milk mixed with sugar should be administered in cases of dysuria (kṛcchra) arising from pitta.
[One should also use] trikaṇṭaka, eraṇḍa, kuśādi, and abhīru...

Ghee prepared with the fresh juice of *karkāruka* and sugarcane, combined with half a part of jaggery, should be drunk for the sake of curing dysuria, urinary calculi, and urinary obstruction. || 28 ||
One *tulā* of *punarnavā* root, along with *daśamūla*, *śatāvarī*, *balā*, *turagagandhā*, *tṛṇamūla*, *trikaṇṭaka*,
*vidārīgandhā*, *nāgāhvā*, *guḍūcī*, and likewise *atibalā*. || 29 ||

One should boil ten *pala* portions each of these separately in one *droṇa* of water. When reduced to one-fourth, one should cook half an *āḍhaka* of ghee with *madhuka*, ginger, grapes, rock salt, and long pepper.
One should separately add two *palas* each of the other grains and one *kuḍava* of barley;
then, having added thirty *palas* of jaggery and one *prastha* of castor oil,
one should stir it well and cook it over a gentle fire.
This is the blameless food to be eaten first by the sons of lords, by kings, those equal to kings, and those who have many wives;
it is also for those suffering from dysuria, stiffness of the waist, and those with constipation. (33–34)
It is recommended for pain in the penis and groin, for pain in the vagina, and for the aforementioned types of abdominal tumors (gulma), as well as those caused by vāta and blood.
It is strengthening, an elixir (rasāyana), cooling, and beneficial for the delicate and the young.
One *droṇa* of *punarnavā* should be added to a hundred [pala] of the decoction; the same applies to other [herbs].
(36) One should conquer urinary obstructions (*mūtrāghāta*) according to the specific *doṣa* using remedies that alleviate dysuria (*mūtrakṛcchra*).
One should administer an enema (basti) and a urethral enema (uttarabasti), as well as an unctuous purgative.
By drinking one akṣa measure of the paste of ervāru seeds mixed with rock salt and fermented grain-water (dhānyāmla), one is indeed liberated from urinary obstruction (mūtrāghāta).
One should drink wine mixed with the barks of *pāṭalī*, *yavaśūka*, and *pāribhadra*, along with sesame, salt water, and *tvak*, *elā*, and *uṣaṇa*;
or one may lick these same ingredients individually, using jaggery as a vehicle.
Or one should cause him to drink salt mixed with the paste of the three myrobalans (triphalā).
One should drink the fresh juice of nidigdhikā strained through a cloth,
or a paste of saffron steeped in water overnight along with honey.
A man suffering from urinary obstruction (mūtrāghāta) should drink the ash of *pāṭalā* mixed with oil, or strained alkaline water, or wine containing *sauvarcala* salt;
or he may take the seeds of the best *elā* together with ginger and pomegranate juice.
Having drunk wine mixed with salt, one is freed from urinary obstruction (mūtraghāta).
One should drink [this] in a decoction of śilājatu, or in the juice of the vīratarādi group, or in the decoction of durālabhā, or in that of vāsaka.
Alternatively, milk prepared with *trikaṇṭaka*, castor root, and *śatāvarī*, or with the five grass roots (*tṛṇapañcamūla*),
thickened with jaggery and mixed with ghee, [is beneficial].
This is recommended for diseases such as those involving difficulty in urination;
one should drink the decoction of the roots of *nalaka*, *kuśa*, *kāśa*, and sugarcane, boiled and well-cooled in the morning.
"Retention of urine will certainly come upon one who drinks [this]," so said Kaca;
[he spoke of] the root of the *godhāvatī*.
When boiled and mixed with ghee, oil, and cow's milk, this [medicine], when drunk, quickly breaks up the obstruction of the accumulation of urine. || 11 ||
The seed of *khadirī* taken with water removes urinary obstruction and calculi;
likewise, the root of *trijaṭā* drunk with buttermilk serves the same purpose.
When urine is obstructed, one should insert camphor powder into the penis.

One should eat boiled rice with milk that has been cooled, and drink sandalwood paste mixed with rice-water and sugar; this is excellent for hot wind (ūṣṇavāta) accompanied by blood. A cold immersion bath and an enema (ābasti) are remedies for the alleviation of hot wind.
Furthermore, the juice of *kūṣmāṇḍaka* (bottle gourd), drunk with alkali and sugar,
is beneficial for one whose blood is discharged due to excessive sexual indulgence; for such a person, abstaining from intercourse and a nourishing regimen are advised.

Take equal parts of *svaguptā* fruit, raisins, black sugarcane juice, and powdered sugar; add half-parts each of milk, honey, and ghee. Having thoroughly churned all these together, one should lick a measure of one *akṣa* and drink milk.
It destroys the disorders arising from the seminal receptacle and bestows a son upon the barren woman.
Citraka, śārivā, balā, kālānuśārivā,
drākṣā, viśālā, pippalī, and likewise citraphalā— [these constitute the formulation].
In the same manner, one should add madhuka and āmalakas;
one should cook an āḍhaka of ghee with these pastes, each measuring one akṣa, in one droṇa of milk and one droṇa of water, and once it is prepared, one should remove it from the heat.
A wise person should mix together cold, strained [milk] combined with one prastha of sugar and *tugākṣīrī*;
then, at the appropriate time, one should drink it in measured amounts according to the specific humor (*doṣa*) and one's own strength.
One who has semen characterized by vāta, pitta, or kapha,
as well as one whose semen is bloody or nodular, should drink this highly efficacious ghee, which is vitalizing, aphrodisiac, and restores health.
A woman who employs this ghee— which is beneficial for progeny, auspicious, a remover of all diseases, and propitious— will obtain a fetus without delay.
It also conquers disorders of the blood and combined disorders of the female reproductive tract.
In all disorders of urine, one should employ this treatment.
(Adhikāra 33) Take the excellent bark of *Varuṇa* combined with *śuṇṭhī* and *gokṣura*.
Having added barley-alkali and jaggery, one should boil it and drink it when beneficial;
this destroys even long-standing urinary calculi born of Vāta.
Vīratara, sahacarī, darbha, vṛkṣādanī, and nala [are used for this].
Gundrā, ākāśa, kuśa, avaśma, bheda, moraṭa, ṭuṇṭuka,
kuruṇṭikā, vaśira, vasuka, and agnimantha; || 3 || indīvarī, śvadaṃṣṭrā, and likewise kāpotavaktraka.
This group, beginning with vīratara and others, removes disorders of vāta;
it cures urinary calculi, gravel, dysuria, and pain caused by trauma.
[It is prepared] with ginger (śuṇṭhī), agnimantha, pāṣāṇabheda, śigru, varuṇa, and gokṣura.
A wise person should prepare a decoction with *abhayā* and the fruits of *āragvadha*; having added powdered asafoetida, alkali, and salt, a man should drink it.
This is an excellent digestive, a stimulant of the appetite, and a destroyer of urinary calculi and dysuria.
It destroys the vāta located in the abdominal cavity and that which has spread to the waist, thighs, anus,
and penis. Pāṣāṇabheda, vasuka, vaśira, aśmantaka, śatāvarī, śvadaṃṣṭrā, bṛhatī, and kaṇṭakārikā [are used for this purpose].
Kapota-vaktra, ārtagala, kāñcana, uśīra, gulmaka, vṛkṣādanī, bhallūka, and the fruit of the varuṇa tree;
barley, kulattha, kola, and the fruits of the kataka tree.
Ghee boiled with a decoction of these [drugs] along with a paste of uṣaka and others quickly breaks up a stone (aśmarī) produced by vāta. Furthermore,
alkaline preparations, barley gruels, thin porridges, decoctions, and milks [are beneficial].
One should also consume foods that alleviate vāta within this group.
Usaka, saindhava salt, hiṅgu, the two types of kāśīsa, guggulu, śilājatu, and tutthaka— this is declared as the usakādi group.
The group beginning with *uśaka* destroys *kapha*, purifies the fat (*medas*),
and cures urinary calculi, gravel, dysuria, colic, and *kaphaja* abdominal tumors (*gulma*). *Kuśa*, *kāśa*, *śara*, *itkara*, *moraṭa*, and *aśmabhit* [perform the same].
Darbha, vidārī, vārāhī, śāli-root, trikaṇṭaka, bhallūka, pāṭalī, pāṭhā, pattūra, then kuruṇṭikā,
the two kinds of punarnavā, and śirīṣa— having boiled these, [an oil] is prepared in them. || 14–15 ||
Clarified butter boiled with the substances known as śilāhvā and madhuka, along with the seeds of indīvara, or the seeds of trapuṣa and vāruka, when administered,
quickly breaks up a stone (aśmarī) produced from bile.
One should prepare alkaline gruels, thin gruels, decoctions, milks,
and meals using this Pitta-subduing group [of drugs].
Likewise, one may use the Varuṇaka-group and others, along with guggulu, elā, and hareṇu.
Ghee prepared from goat’s milk with kuṣṭha, mustā, marica, citraka, and surāhvaya,
along with the uṣakādi group of drugs, quickly breaks up stones produced by kapha.
In this group that destroys kapha, one should prepare alkaline preparations, barley gruels, thin decoctions, milks, and foods.
Taruṇārtagala, śigru, tarkārī, and madhuśigruka [are included].
Meṣaśṛṅgī, karañja, bimba, agnimantha, moraṭā,
the two types of śairīya, śirīṣa, darbha, varī, vasuka, citraka, bilva, ajaśṛṅgī, and the two types of bṛhatī. || 21–22 ||
Indeed, this group beginning with Varuṇa wards off phlegm and fat; it destroys headache, abdominal tumors (gulma), and internal abscesses (vidradhi).
Furthermore, a decoction of Varuṇa bark drunk together with jaggery [is likewise beneficial].
It causes stones to fall away quickly and relieves pain in the bladder.
One should drink alkali of barley mixed with jaggery, along with the juice derived from flowers and fruits, which destroys urinary obstruction and dissolves gravel and stones.
One should drink a decoction of the bark of Varuṇa roots combined with its paste;
likewise, a slightly warm decoction derived from Śigru roots destroys urinary calculi.
[26] [The paste of] Nāgara, Varuṇa, and Gokṣura...
A decoction made from *pāṣāṇabheda*, *kapota*, and *valka*, when drunk mixed with jaggery and *yavaśūka*, destroys even severe urinary calculi. || 27 ||
A decoction prepared from *varuṇatvak*, *śilābheda*, *śuṇṭhī*,
and *gokṣuraka*, combined with alkali, breaks up even gravel. [Likewise,] *śvadaṃṣṭrā*, castor leaves, *nāgara*, and *varuṇatvak* [are used].

One should drink this excellent decoction in the morning to break up urinary calculi. [Likewise, one may take] the roots of śvadaṃṣṭrā, kṣuraka, uruvūka, and the two types of bṛhatī, ground with milk.
Having stirred it with sweet curd,
it should be drunk for seven days for the purpose of breaking up urinary calculi.
The juice of ripe *ikṣvāku* mixed with alkali and sugar removes urinary calculi.
Wine mixed with *sauvarcala* salt overcomes the affliction of stone-like diseases (*pāṣāṇaroga*);
likewise, [a mixture of] honey, milk, and the ash of sesame stalks for three nights [does so].
[Also effective are] *elā*, *upakulyā*, *madhuka*, and *aśmabheda*.
In cases of urinary calculi and dysuria, one should drink a decoction of kauntī, īṣad-daṃṣṭrā, vṛṣaka, and uruvūka, enriched with ashmaja-tu and sugar.
One should drink for seven days the powder of *trikaṇṭaka* seeds mixed with honey and sheep’s milk; this destroys urinary calculi.
In cases of seminal calculus (*śukrāśmarī*), however, the general procedure for destroying calculi is to be applied.
Pāṣāṇabheda, vṛṣaka, śvadaṃṣṭrā,
pāṭhā, abhayā, vyoṣa, śaṭhī, nikumbha, hiṃsrā, kharāśvā, and sitamāraka— [these are the ingredients].
The seeds of *mervāruka* and *trapuṣa*; *upakuñcikā*, asafoetida (*hiṅgu*), sour cane-sugar-cane juice (*savetasāmla*),
the two types of *bṛhatī*, *hapuṣā*, and *vacā*.
One should drink the powder that breaks up urinary stones, along with clarified butter cooked with four parts cow's urine and these [drugs]:
kulattha, saindhava salt, and the essence of viḍaṅga. || 36 || 10 ||
One should cook ghee with sugar, śītali, yavaśūka, and the seeds of kūṣmāṇḍaka and gokṣura in the water of nāgavaruṇa.
It quickly destroys all these: difficult-to-cure urinary stones, dysuria, suppression of urine, and urinary retention.

Or one should cook one *prastha* of ghee with the decoction of the five roots beginning with *śara*, together with a paste of *gokṣura*; once prepared, it should be consumed with sugar, like a thunderbolt striking trees that have grown tall. || 38 || 11 ||
It destroys urinary calculi and dysuria, and removes pain from the seminal passage.
One should boil one *tulā* of crushed *varuṇa* in one *droṇa* of water until reduced to one-fourth; having strained it, one should cook one *prastha* of ghee with this decoction.
Varuṇa, kadalī, bilva, the five roots (pañcamūlaka) produced from grass,
amṛtā, stone-born [minerals], and the seed derived from the trapuṣa should be given;
likewise, the lye of śataparvā and sesame, and the lye of palāśa.
One should add one karṣa each of the roots of yūthikā;
the person should drink this dose in consideration of the place, time, and other factors.
When that has been digested, one should first drink jaggery, and once that is digested, [one should drink] buttermilk.
It destroys urinary calculi, gravel, and dysuria.
That oil known as Saindhavādya, which was proclaimed in the section on hernia (bradhna), should be cooked with double the amount of milk along with the Vīratarādi group of drugs.
This excellent and supreme oil, prepared by the best of physicians with the aforementioned decoction and paste, is the destroyer of urinary calculi (aśmarī).
It is likewise effective in cases of urinary obstruction (mūtrāghāta), painful urination (mūtrakṛcchra), slimy urine (picchita), and traumatized urine (mathita).
When [the patient] is broken down and overcome by exhaustion,
it is recommended in every respect to cook oil with a decoction of the bark, leaves, roots, and flowers of *varuṇa* and *satrikaṇṭaka*, for use as a *sthāpana* enema (*basti*).

It destroys gravel, urinary stones, and colic, and prevents dysuria. Having rejected a stone that cannot be pacified by the methods of a surgeon, one should extract it after inserting two fingers into the anus; [this applies to] a stone located between the anus and the penis.
On the left side of the suture, having made an incision leaving a space of one barley-corn, the surgeon skilled in surgical procedures should extract the stone. However,
if the bladder is ruptured due to lack of discernment, death may occur even in the absence of a stone.
One should ensure that the stone is removed without residue and drain the blood from the bladder.

Once the stone has been extracted, one should have the patient immerse himself in warm water and feed him jaggery for the purification of the urine; thereafter, the wound should be smeared with honey and clarified butter.
For three days, one should administer gruel prepared with clarified butter and drugs that purify the urine; thereafter, for ten days, one should give soft rice with milk.
One should apply fomentation using barley and honey, and wash the ulcer with decoctions.
One should apply a plaster made of prapauṇḍarīka, mañjiṣṭhā, yaṣṭi, and lodhra.
Ghee prepared with these same ingredients as a decoction is beneficial for massage.
However, if the ulcer has not subsided after seven days, cauterization (dāha) is also recommended.
But that which has adhered to the navel by chance, one should tear away and remove.
(54) [Adhikāra 34] Śyāmāka, kodrava, uddāla, wheat, chickpeas, and āḍhakī—
Kulattha beans are always beneficial in the diet for those suffering from urinary disorders (meha).
Likewise, meat from wild animals, bitter vegetables, barley-based foods, and honey are recommended.
Furthermore, the individual [medicinal powders] of pārijāta, jayā, nimba, vahnigāyatrī, and [the others] should be used separately.

The eight decoctions of *pāṭhā*, *sāguru*, the two types of *śārada*, water, sugarcane juice, wine, sand, and gradually salted flour, when drunk with honey, successively destroy the various forms of *sāndrameha*. (3)
Dūrvā, kaśeru, pūtīka, puṃbhīka, lava, and śaivala,
boiled with water and drunk, are an excellent remedy for śukra-meha (seminal disorders).
A decoction of triphalā, āragvadha, and drākṣā, combined with honey, [is likewise beneficial].
When drunk, it invariably destroys the urinary disorder known as *phenaprameha* in men.
[This is prepared from] lodhra, abhayā, kaṭphala, mustaka, viḍaṅga, pāṭhā, arjuna, and dhanvana.
These four decoctions— of kadamba, śāla, arjuna, and dīpyaka; and of biḍaṅga, dārvī, dhava, and śallakī— should be taken with honey.
These five decoctions—
prepared from *aśvattha*, *caturaṅgula*, *nyagrodha* and its associates, the three fruits (*phalatrika*),
and *jiṅginī* with red sandalwood (*raktasāra*)— should be consumed with honey in cases of *kapha*-dominant urinary disorders (*kaphaprameha*).

These [decoctions] respectively destroy the urinary disorders known as nīla, daridra, phenākhya, kṣāra, and mañjiṣṭhaka; this decoction made from dates (kharjūra), kāśmarya, the seeds of tinduka, and amṛtā, when mixed with honey, cures raktameha.
Of *lodhra*, *arjuna*, *uśīra*, and *kucandana*;
of *ariṣṭa*, *sevyā*, *āmalaka*, and *abhayā*;
and of *dhātrī*, *arjuna*, *ariṣṭaka*, and *vatsaka*.
These four decoctions— of blue lotus, *elā*, * tiniśa*, and *arjuna*—
are prescribed for urinary disorders with pitta when combined with honey. || 10–11 ||
A person suffering from *sarpirmeha* (ghee-like urine) should drink a powder made by grinding *chinna*, *vahni*, *kaṣāya*, *pāṭhā*, *kuṭaja*, *rāmaṭha*, *tiktā*, and *kuṣṭha*.
For *kṣaudrameha* (honey-like urine), one should drink a decoction of *kadara*, *khadira*, and *pūga*.
One should administer a decoction of agnimantha in cases of vasāmeha.
The physician should administer a decoction of pāṭhā, śirīṣa, dūsparśa, mūrvā, kiṃśuka, tinduka, and kapittha in cases of hastimēha.
Powdered flowers of *kampilā*, *saptacchada*, *śāla*, *vibhītaka*, *rauhītaka*, *kauṭaja*, and *kapittha*.
One suffering from *kapha-pitta* types of urinary disorders (*meha*) should lick [the powder] with honey.
The juice of *dhātrī* (myrobalan) combined with honey and *niśā* (turmeric) cures all types of *meha*; alternatively, a decoction made from *triphalā*, *dāru*, and *mustaka* may be used.
One should drink a decoction of the three fruits (triphalā), darunishā, viśālā, and musta, mixed with a paste of niśā in equal parts and combined with honey.
When all types of *prameha* have arisen,
a decoction prepared with equal parts of *kaṭaṅkaṭerī*, *madhuka*, the three myrobalans (*triphalā*), and *citraka* should be drunk; it is the destroyer of *pramehas*.
A decoction of triphalā, dāru, dārvī, and abda, taken with honey, destroys urinary disorders (meha);
or alternatively, one made from kuṭaja, aśana, dārvī, abda, and the three myrobalans (phalatraya).
Furthermore, the powder of triphalā, iron, śilājatu, and pathyā, when licked, [each individually] [acts as a remedy].
Like the fresh juice of the Madhūka flower, it expels all types of urinary disorders (meha).
One should drink one akṣa of the paste of Śāla, Muṣkaka, and Kampilla with the juice of Dhātrī and honey; this is the supreme remedy for all meha.
Nyagrodha, udumbara, aśvattha, śyonāka, and āragvadha;
āmra, jambu, kapittha, priyāla, kakubha, and dhava; madhūka, madhuka, lodhra, varuṇa, and pāribhadraka. || 22 ||
Paṭola, meṣaśṛṅgī, dantī, citraka, āḍhakī, karañja, the three myrobalans (triphalā), indra (guḍūcī), and bhallātaka fruits—
one should have these made into a fine powder in equal proportions. || 23-24 ||
One should lick this powder, beginning with *nyagrodha*, together with honey, and subsequently drink the juice of the three fruits (*phalatraya*); thus the urine becomes purified.
By this means, the twenty types of urinary disorders (*meha*) and those conditions of dysuria (*mūtrakṛcchra*) are cured.
By means of this yoga, swellings are pacified and no new ones arise;
furthermore, in this case, the bones of the *nyagrodha*, *āmra*, and *jambu* are taken,
along with *trikaṇṭaka*, *aśmantaka*, and *somavalka*.
With bhallātaka, ativiṣā, and lodhra;
with vacā, paṭola, arjuna, nimba, musta, haridrā, dīpyaka, and padmaka. || 27 ||
One should cook oil or ghee with mañjiṣṭhā, pāṭhā, aguru, and candana— all these ingredients combined— to treat urinary disorders caused by kapha and vāta.
When the three types of pitta are mixed with their respective symptoms, [the treatment is as follows]:
ghee prepared with a decoction that cures kapha-type urinary disorders is beneficial for kapha;
ghee prepared with a decoction that cures pitta-type urinary disorders is beneficial for pitta. || 29 ||
The ten roots (daśamūla), the two types of karañja, devadāru, harītakī, varṣābhū, varuṇa, dantī, citraka, and punarnavā;
as well as sudhā, nīpa, kadamba, bilva, and bhallātaka. || 30 ||
One should cook ten *pala* portions each of *śaṭhī*, *puṣkaramūla*, and *pippalīmūla* in one *āḍhaka* of water; then,
one should add one *prastha* each of *yava*, *kola*, and *kulattha*.
With that residue of one-quarter [of the original quantity], one should cook one *prastha* of clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
[The decoction should be made from] *nicula*, the three myrobalans (*triphalā*), *bhārgī*, *rohiṣa*, *gajapippalī*, *śṛṅgavera*, *viḍaṅga*, *vacā*, and likewise *kampillaka*.
Once this is prepared, one should have it drunk by the pregnant woman according to her strength;
this is the celebrated and excellent ghee known as Dhānvantara.
It cures skin diseases, abdominal tumors, urinary disorders, edema, and gout.

This ghee cures splenic enlargement, hemorrhoids, abscesses, and those various types of carbuncles, as well as epilepsy and insanity. In that case, one should cook one hundred parts each of the medicinal substances separately in water and in ghee.
In addition to three hundred [units], water should be added according to the procedure for pouring out.

Then, the physician should prepare pills by combining guggulu with an equal amount of the powder of the three pungents (trikaṭu) and the three myrobalans (triphalā), mixed with a decoction of gokṣuraka. || 36–37 ||
One should consume the purgative medicine after considering the humors, the season, and one's strength;
there is no restriction here, and one may perform the action as desired.
It conquers urinary disorders (prameha), obstructions of urine (mūtraghāta), diseases of children, and abdominal enlargements (udara). || 38 ||
One whose body has been thoroughly purified should drink śilājatu that has been infused with the decoction of śālasāra and other such woods, ground into a paste according to one's strength;
and when that has been digested, the meal should be taken together with the juices of wild (jāṅgala) animals.
A person should continue this practice in this manner until they have consumed the entire quantity of the balance; having abandoned diabetes (madhumeha), as well as gravel and urinary stones,
he shall live for a hundred years free from disease, endowed with physical beauty, complexion, and strength.

Iron [preparation] combined with viḍaṅga, triphalā, musta, kaṇā, nāgara, and the two types of jīraka destroys even the most difficult urinary disorders (prameha) and all urinary abnormalities; of this there is no doubt. (42)
In this same manner, one should also employ the mākṣika mineral; its quality is as follows:
when the decoction of the śālasārādi group has reached a thick consistency, one should add the powders of dantī, lodhra, śivā, kāntaloha, and copper.
By consuming it when thickened and not yet burnt, one overcomes urinary disorders.
By engaging in all forms of physical exercise, one overcomes urinary disorders;
likewise, by living like a sage—eating alms-food and remaining without shoes or an umbrella—one overcomes them.
One who subsists on wild rice and *āmalaka* fruits may, by means of physical strength, travel a hundred *yojanas* or even more continuously in order to conquer urinary disorders (*meha*).
A physician should treat swellings such as *śarāvikā* and others in the same manner as other types of edema.
Once they have matured, one should treat them like ulcers;
for their internal consumption, a decoction of *vanaspati* mixed with goat's urine is recommended for cleansing the ulcer.
One should also prepare an oil with the *elādika* group of drugs for the healing of the ulcer.
One should prepare a decoction with *āragvadha* and other drugs, as well as medicinal rubs (*udvartana*),
affusions (*seka*) with *śālasāra* and other substances, and food and other items prepared with *kaṇā* (long pepper) and others.
[One may also use] *sauvīraka*, liquor, *śukta*, oil, milk, ghee, and jaggery.
One should avoid foods ground with sour gruel and sugarcane juice, as well as the meat of animals from marshy regions.
(50) Chapter 35:
One who is fond of physical exertion, anxiety, sexual intercourse, walking long distances, honey, and staying awake at night;
One who subsists on a diet of barley and śyāmāka grain will inevitably destroy excessive corpulence.
One who desires to abandon corpulence should gradually and progressively increase the avoidance of sleep, sexual intercourse, physical exercise, and mental anxieties.
Water mixed with honey consumed in the morning destroys obesity;
or, by drinking hot rice-scum (*maṇḍa*), one becomes lean of body.
[The powder of] *cavya*, *jīraka*, *vyoṣa*, *hiṅgu*, *sauvarcala*, and *anala*—
Barley flour drunk with mastu destroys fat and stimulates the digestive fire.
A preparation consisting of viḍaṅga, ginger, alkali, iron filings, honey, barley, and āmalaka powder is a remedy for the destruction of obesity.
Vyoṣa, viḍaṅga, śigru, triphalā, kaṭurohiṇī,
the two types of bṛhatī, the two types of haridrā, pāṭhā, ativiṣā, sthirā, hiṅgu, kebukamūla, yamānī, dhānya, and citraka.
One should powder together sauvarcala salt, ajājī, and hapuṣā.
The portions of the powder, oil, ghee, and honey should be equal in measure; to these, one should add sixteen times the amount of flour and drink it as a nourishing tonic (saṃtarpaṇa).
Through its application, diseases arising from over-nutrition (santarpaṇa) are pacified,
as well as urinary disorders (prameha), obstructed winds (mūḍhavāta), skin diseases (kuṣṭha),
hemorrhoids (arśas), jaundice (kāmalā), splenic enlargement, anemia, edema, dysuria, and anorexia.
Heart disease, consumption (rājayakṣmā), cough, asthma, throat obstructions, worms, disorders of the digestive tract (grahaṇī), excessive paleness, and extreme obesity [are cured];
furthermore, the digestive fire of men is kindled, and memory and intelligence arise. || 10–11 ||
A gruel prepared with *kāñjika* and a paste of *badarī* leaves overcomes obesity; likewise, *śilājatu* combined with the juice of *agnimantha*,
or [a preparation of] *amṛtā*, *truṭi*, *vella*, and *vatsaka*.

Kaliṅga, pathyā, āmalaka, and guggulu— this [mixture], increased in sequence and saturated with honey, conquers eruptions (piḍakā), enlargement [of the anus] (sthaulya), and fistula-in-ano (bhagaṇḍara). || 13 ||
By consuming guggulu in equal parts with the three pungents (vyoṣa), agni, triphalā, musta, and viḍaṅga,
one conquers all diseases born of fat, phlegm, and wind. Guggulu, tālamūlī, triphalā, khadira, and vṛṣa— [these are used together].
Trivṛt, ālambuṣā, snuk, nirguṇḍī, and likewise citraka—
of these, one should take ten palas each and boil them in five āḍhakas of water; having reduced it to one-fourth, one should then remove the decoction from the heat.
Twelve *pala*s of finely powdered sharp iron (*tīkṣṇalauha*) should be given,
along with one *prastha* of aged clarified butter (*purāṇasarpiṣaḥ*) and eight *pala*s of sugar;
these should be cooked in a copper vessel and then removed once it has become well-cooled.
Half a *prastha* of honey should be added, along with two *palas* of *śilājatu*.
Half a *pala* each of cardamom and cinnamon, two *palas* of *viḍaṅga*, black pepper, *añjana*, and two *palas* of long pepper, combined with the three myrobalans (*triphalā*).
Two palas of *kāśīsa* (green vitriol), finely ground into powder by the wise, should be added to the [mixture], well-stirred, and placed in a smooth vessel. Then,
one whose body has been thoroughly purified should consume a dose the size of an *akṣa*.
One should drink milk as a post-drink (anupāna), or likewise the broth of wild animals;
it is excellent for removing wind and phlegm, and cures skin diseases, urinary disorders, abdominal enlargements, jaundice, anemia, edema, and fistula-in-ano.
Fasting is the best remedy for various conditions such as fainting, delusion, poisoning, insanity, and artificial poisons; it is the supreme medicine for those who are corpulent.
One should excessively emaciate the belly until it resembles the depths of the underworld.
It is strengthening, an elixir, intellect-promoting, and a supreme aphrodisiac;
it brings prosperity, produces sons, and destroys wrinkles and graying hair.
One should not eat the root of the plantain, sour gruel, or the karamarda fruit.
One should avoid the *karīra* fruit and the *kāravella* gourd; these are the six things beginning with the letter *ka*.
[25] [One should take] *triphalā*, *ativiṣā*, *mūrvā*, *trivṛt*, *citraka*, and *vāsaka*;
[and] *nimba*, *āragvadha*, *ṣaṭgrantha*, *saptaparṇa*, and the two types of *niśā*. [26]
Oil cooked with equal parts of guḍūcī, indrasurā, kṛṣṇā, kuṣṭha, sarṣapa, and nāgara, and saturated with the juice of the surasādi group,
when employed for drinking, massage, gargling, nasal drops, and enemas— || 27 ||
One should conquer diseases of the skin and throat caused by phlegm by using *sthūlatāla*.
A bath with *śirīṣa*, *lāmajjaka*, *hema*,
and *lodhra* removes skin disorders and excessive perspiration, bringing great delight.
A medicinal paste (pradeha) consisting of patra, ambu, lauha, abhayā, and candana removes foul body odor.
A plaster made from the juice of half a vāsā leaf combined with powdered conch-shell likewise [removes it].
Or else, the juice of bilva leaves destroys bodily foul odors.
[The paste of] harītakī, lodhra, mariṣṭa leaves,
mango bark, and pomegranate rind [is also used for this].
This is declared to be the body-paste for women and the leg-decoction for kings. [It is made from] the light Malaya-born [sandalwood] that is as delicate as water droplets on a petal... 31.
This ointment removes the foul odor of the body,
like powdered *ālambuṣā* drunk together with pure *araṇāla*. 32.
Ground with cow urine, it destroys leprosy; when combined with cow’s milk, it produces a radiant complexion;
and with [cow’s] milk, it removes foul odors from the armpits and other areas.
It is recommended for subjugation by means of the two types of *rajanī*.
An ointment made from the fresh juice of *ciñcā* leaves mixed with burnt turmeric and applied to the armpits and other areas quickly overcomes the foul odor of the body.
One should apply *guggulu* and the five bitter herbs (*pañcatiktaka*) to the hands and feet;
alternatively, one should unweariedly consume the clarified butter known as *pañcatiktaghṛta*.
(35) Chapter 36.
Since the digestive fire is weak when the stomach and abdomen are filled with morbid humors (doṣas),
one should therefore employ foods that are appetizing and light.
[These include] red śāli rice, barley, mung beans, and the meat of wild animals and birds.
One should likewise drink fermented liquors made from milk, urine, water, or molasses, as well as honey-sweetened drinks (madhuśīdhu).
For a strong patient with vātodara, one should first treat them with unctuous substances; once the body has been lubricated and fomented, one should administer an unctuous purgative.
Once the morbid humor has been removed and the abdomen has become flaccid, one should wrap it with a cloth;
thus, due to the lack of space, the air will cause it to expand again.
This occurs because of the excessive administration of therapies for the humors and the resulting obstruction of the channels.
Therefore, the abdomen becomes distended; hence, one should always administer purgation to this patient.

Once purged, a person suffering from *vātodara* (wind-belly) should drink a decoction of *peyā* (thin gruel) prepared with drugs that alleviate the specific *doṣas*, or he should drink *takra* (buttermilk) mixed with *pippalī* and salt.

One suffering from *pitta*-dominated abdominal enlargement (*pittodara*) should drink it sweetened with sugar and black pepper; one suffering from *kapha*-dominated abdominal enlargement (*kaphodara*) should take it combined with *yamānī*, rock salt, cumin, and the three pungents (*tryūṣaṇa*).
One should drink buttermilk mixed with honey, clearly sour, and not too thin.

One suffering from *plīhodara* (enlarged spleen) should take it combined with honey, oil, *vacā*, ginger, *śatāhvā*, *kuṣṭha*, and rock salt (*saindhava*). One suffering from *dakodara* (ascites) should take it with the three pungents (*vyoṣa*). However, one suffering from *baddhodara* (intestinal obstruction) should take it with *hapuṣā*, *dīpyaka*, cumin (*ajāji*), and rock salt.
A woman with dropsical abdomen (chidrodarī) should drink buttermilk mixed with long pepper and honey;
one with abdominal enlargement due to the accumulation of doshas (nicayodarī) should take it combined with the three pungents (tryūṣaṇa), alkali, and salt.
This is for those suffering from heaviness, anorexia, weak digestion, and diarrhea.
Buttermilk is prescribed as nectar for those afflicted by wind (vāta) and phlegm (kapha).
For abdominal enlargement caused by wind (vātodara), there should be a practice of drinking milk and a decoction enema (nirūha) made from the ten roots (daśamūla);
for enlargement with constipation (sodāvarta), an oil enema (anuvāsana) should be administered using castor oil boiled with wind-alleviating sour substances.
Sāmudra salt, sauvarcala salt, saindhava salt, barley alkali, ajamoda, long pepper,
citraka, and ginger;
One should prepare equal parts of asafoetida and biḍa salt;
these powders, saturated with ghee, should be eaten, preceded by a recommended gargle.
It cures wind-induced abdominal enlargement (vātodara), abdominal tumors (gulma), indigestion from eating,
provocation of the bodily wind (vāyu), and morbid dysentery (grahaṇī); it also treats malignant hemorrhoids and jaundice (pāṇḍuroga).
And it destroys fistula-in-ano immediately.

In the case of pitta-type abdominal enlargement (pittodara), one should first administer a purgative to a strong patient; however, a weak patient should be given an oil enema (anuvāsana), purified by a milk enema (kṣīrabasti), and then purged.
One who has been purified from *kapha*-derived abdominal enlargement should be fed milk mixed with the paste of *sativṛt*, or with *urubūka* boiled [with milk],
or with *śātalā* and *trāyamāṇā* boiled [with milk], or with *āragvadha* boiled [with milk]; and he should be given pungent foods,
alkaline substances, and grain-based meals.

One should also administer urine-based fermented liquors (ariṣṭas) and iron preparations that alleviate kapha. In the case of abdominal enlargement caused by the derangement of all three humors (sannipātōdara), one should perform every treatment previously described.
In splenic enlargement (plīhodara), one should apply treatments that cure the spleen as well as those that cure abdominal enlargement in general.

To one who has undergone sudation and suffers from abdominal distension, one should administer a non-unctuous enema (nirūha) containing urine, sharp medicinal drugs, oil, and salt, followed by an unctuous enema (anuvāsana). Furthermore, one should prescribe foods that cause laxity as well as strong purgatives.

In cases of *chidrodara* (perforated abdomen), one should treat it like *śleṣmodara* (kaphaja abdominal enlargement) after applying sudation (*sveda*). Whenever fluid accumulates, it should be drained; surgical intervention (*śastrakarma*) as prescribed in the scriptures should also be performed.
In *jalodara* (ascites), one must especially avoid the consumption of liquids.
One should gently apply a plaster to the abdomen using *devadāru*, *palāśa*, *arka*, *hastipippalī*, and *śigru*, along with *aśvagandhā* and cow's urine.
One should employ the eight types of urine for both sprinkling and internal consumption by those suffering from abdominal enlargement (*udarin*).

One suffering from abdominal disease should consume milk while subsisting on a diet of milk, and should administer one thousand *pippalī* fruits that have been processed with the milky sap of the *snuhī* plant according to their capacity;
likewise, [one should use] *śilājatu*, the various urines, *guggulu*, and the three myrobalans (*triphalā*).
The application of Snuhī milk also pacifies abdominal disease;
a filtered preparation made from rice powder thoroughly saturated with the milk of Snuhī destroys even a massive abdomen within seven nights. (26)
Or one should employ the *pippalīvardhamāna* (the increasing dose of long pepper) as prescribed in the medical compendium (*kalpa*);
there is nothing on earth equal to it for the destruction of abdominal enlargements (*jaṭhara*).
[One may also use] the root of *paṭola*, turmeric, *viḍaṅga*, and the bark of the three myrobalans (*triphalā*).
One should powder kampillaka, nīlinī, and trivṛt; taking six karṣas of the first [drug], one karṣa of the second, and three, two, and four karṣas respectively of the last three,
one should then take a handful of this powder with cow's urine and drink it.
Once purged, he should eat soft rice with the meat-broth of wild animals (jāṅgala).
After drinking thin gruel and thick gruel, he should drink milk boiled for six days with the three pungents (vyoṣa);
he should likewise drink that powder repeatedly in this manner.
This powder destroys all types of abdominal enlargements, even those accompanied by ascites; it also removes jaundice, anemia, and edema. [32] 6. Yamānī, hapuṣā, dhānya, triphalā, and upakuñcikā.
Kāravī, pippalīmūla, ajagandhā,
śaṭhī, vacā, śatāhvā, jīraka, vyoṣa, svarṇakṣīrī, citraka, the two alkalis (kṣārau), pauṣkaramūla, kuṣṭha, and the five salts (lavaṇapañcaka). || 33–34 ||
Take equal parts of viḍaṅga, three parts of dantī, twice as much (two parts) each of trivṛt and viśālā, and four times as much śātalā. This powder, named Nārāyaṇa, destroys hosts of diseases.

Having obtained this, diseases do not increase, just as the Asuras did not prosper upon reaching Viṣṇu. It should be drunk with buttermilk by those suffering from abdominal enlargements, with pomegranate juice by those with abdominal tumors,
with liquor in cases of obstructed wind, and with clear wine in diseases of the wind-humor.
In cases of constipation, one should use whey; in hemorrhoids and cutting pain, pomegranate juice; in indigestion, sour wood-apple with warm water;
and in fistula-in-ano, anemia, cough, asthma, and throat-obstruction [these remedies should be applied].

In cases of heart disease, disorders of the duodenum (grahaṇī), sluggish digestive fire in the gastrointestinal tract, and fever; in cases of venom from fangs, root-venoms, natural poisons, and artificial poisons—
this purgative should be drunk as appropriate by one whose bowels have been lubricated.
One should drink the paste of dantī, vacā, gavākṣī, śaṅkhinī, tilvaka, and trivṛt with cow urine to destroy abdominal diseases.
A person who has abstained from food should drink buffalo urine mixed with milk.
By this, the abdominal enlargement is pacified within seven days; of this there is no doubt.
For the destruction of all types of *udara*, one should drink cow’s urine combined with a paste of *gavākṣī*, *śaṅkhinī*, *dantī*, and *nīlinī*. (42–43)
Then, one should burn *arka* leaves with salt in a smokeless fire;
subsequently, one should drink that [ash] with whey and milk, which removes abdominal tumors (*gulma*) and splenic enlargement (*plīhodara*).
When drunk along with long pepper (*pippalī*) and black pepper (*marica*), it destroys splenic enlargement.
A decoction of drumstick tree (śigru) combined with amlavetasa and rock salt;
for one who has lost consciousness, having administered this and then cast the root of indravāruṇī far away, his splenic enlargement (plīhodara) is pacified. (45–46)

Urine or water saturated with the powder of *rohitaka*, *abhayā*, and *akṣa*, when drunk, cures all types of abdominal enlargements, splenic disorders, urinary diseases, hemorrhoids, worms, and abdominal tumors.
[47] Devadruma, *śigru*, and *mayūraka*— [Note: This fragment appears to be the beginning of verse 48.]
Alternatively, having drunk ashwagandha ground with cow's urine, one will quickly destroy enlarged abdomen, worms, swelling, and vitiated abdominal disease. || 48 ||
A decoction of the ten roots (daśamūla), ginger (nāgara), chinnaruhā, punarnavā,
and abhayā conquers ascites and edema.
It also cures elephantiasis, goiters, and diseases caused by vāta.
A decoction of *harītakī*, ginger, *devadāru*, *punarnavā*, and *chinnaruhā* [achieves this].
Guggulu mixed with urine should be drunk; this is an excellent treatment for swellings and abdominal enlargements (śothodara).
Castor oil mixed with daśamūla [is also recommended].
The juice of triphalā mixed with cow’s urine, or a decoction of daśamūla combined with cow’s urine, destroys vātodara, swelling, and colic. (51)
A decoction of punarnavā, nimba, paṭola,
śuṇṭhī, tiktā, abhayā, dāru, and amṛtā [remedies] swelling of the entire body, abdominal enlargement, cough, and colic.
It destroys anemia accompanied by dyspnea.
One should drink *punarnavā*, *dāruharidrā*, and *guḍūcī* together with cow urine and *mahiṣākṣa*.
In cases of skin diseases, swelling, abdominal enlargement, anemia, obesity, excessive salivation, and disorders of upward-moving phlegm,
[one should take] buffalo milk mixed with cow urine. || 53 ||
For cases of swelling and abdominal enlargement, one should drink cow's milk mixed with triphalā, or simply cow's milk alone, or indeed only cow's urine, after having consumed a meal of milk-rice.
One should powder equal parts of punarnavā, dāru, amṛtā, pāṭhā, bilva, śvadaṃṣṭrikā, the two types of bṛhatī, the two types of rañjanī, pippalī, citraka, and vṛṣa, and drink it with cow’s urine. (55)
It destroys swelling of many kinds that spreads through all the limbs, as well as the eight types of colic and abdominal ailments, and even severe ulcers.
[One should prepare this] by grinding old *māṇaka* seeds with twice the amount of rice flour.
One should then practice this prepared milk-rice (pāyasa) with milk and water.
This proven method, declared by physicians to be free from harm, destroys wind-belliedness (vātodara), swelling, malabsorption syndrome (grahaṇī), and even jaundice (pāṇḍutā).
Half a *pātra* of ghee prepared with half a *tulā* of the decoction of the ten roots (*daśamūla*), along with one *pala* each of the five spices (*pañcakola*) and alkali (*kṣāra*).
This preparation, containing two *mastuka* fruits, destroys abdominal tumors and swellings.
One suffering from abdominal disease should drink one *prastha* of clarified butter prepared with four parts water, two parts urine, and a paste of one *pala* of *citraka*, along with alkali. (59–60)
Two palas of *arka* milk, six palas of *snuhī* milk, along with *pathyā*, *kampillaka*, *śyāmā*, *sampāka*, *girikarṇikā*, *nīlinī*,
*trivṛtā*, *dantī*, *śaṅkhinī*, and likewise *citraka*.
One should cook one prastha of ghee with the pala-measures of these [ingredients].
Then, if his digestive tract (koṣṭha) is impure, one should administer it drop by drop; for as many drops as he drinks, so many times will he undergo purgation.
It pacifies leprosy, abdominal tumors, upward movement of wind (udāvarta), swelling, fistula-in-ano, and the eight types of abdominal enlargements, just as Indra’s thunderbolt destroys a tree;
this is known as Bindu-ghee, by anointing with which one is purged. (64)

One should drink a dose of one *prastha* of ghee prepared with one *āḍhaka* of whey (*dadhimanda*) and one *pala* of the paste of *snuk*-milk for the pacification of abdominal enlargement (*jaṭhara*).
Likewise, one should drink one *prastha* of ghee prepared with eight times as much milk.
With a paste of one pala of snuk-milk and six palas of trivṛt;
[or] combined with a paste of snuk-milk, dantī, triphalā, viḍaṅga, siṃhī, trivṛt, and citraka.
Having drunk one *kuḍava* measure of clarified butter cooked with water, or half a *karṣa* of it,
one should drink warm water after it has been digested; when purged, [one should follow this regimen].
One who knows the procedure should administer lukewarm gruel;
this "iron arrow" (nārāca) is prescribed as a remedy for abdominal diseases when used in the proper measure.
Chapter 37:
[The treatment] of *iyamānikā*, *citraka*, *yavaśūka*, *ṣaḍgranthi*, *dantī*, and those originating from Magadha.
This powder destroys the spleen when taken with warm water, or with buttermilk, wine, or fermented liquor.
One should administer long pepper that has been saturated with the alkali of *kiṃśuka* flowers.
It destroys abdominal tumors (gulma) and splenic enlargement, stimulates the digestive fire, and acts as a rejuvenative (rasāyana).
Having burnt Viḍaṅga, ghee, Agni, Sindhūttha, and flour, along with Vacā, one should drink them after pulverizing the mixture with milk; this removes abdominal tumors and splenic enlargement.
Alkali derived from *tāla* flowers, taken with jaggery, destroys splenic enlargement;

or one should drink in the morning, according to one's strength, the alkali of *pūtīka* extracted with sour liquids along with *viḍa* salt and long pepper (*kṛṣṇā*), for the purpose of pacifying the spleen and liver.
An alkaline preparation derived from oyster shells should be drunk with milk according to the proper method;
or, long peppers (pippalī) should be administered with milk for the pacification of splenic enlargement (plīha).
A bolus (modaka) made of marking-nut (bhallātaka), chebulic myrobalan (abhayā), and cumin (jājī) together with jaggery [is also effective].

A decoction of *śobhāñjana* combined with rock salt (*saindhava*), black pepper (*agnikaṇā*), and the alkali of *palāśa* or barley alkali (*yavākṣāra*) quickly destroys even the most formidable splenomegaly within seven nights. (7)
Two *tila* seeds with salt, as well as six *pala* of ghee;
one should employ all the treatments prescribed for spleen disease (*plīha*) for liver disease (*yakṛt*) as well.
One should also consume garlic, the root of long pepper (*pippalī*), and *abhayā*.
One should drink a mouthful of cow’s urine for the relief of splenic disease (*plīharoga*).
A paste of *śarapuṅkhā*, which cures the spleen, should be consumed with buttermilk;
or else, having chewed *śarapuṅkhā* itself, one should eat it followed by a drink of *abhayā*.
A decoction of śārṅgeṣṭhā with saindhava salt mixed with tintiḍīka is a formulation for the alleviation of splenic enlargement (plīha), or alternatively, the juice of ripe mango with honey [is used].
After the patient has eaten with curd, the physician [should open] a vein in the middle of the left arm.
One should pierce [the spleen] on the left for the destruction of the spleen, and on the right for the destruction of the liver.
One should firmly massage the spleen to induce the flow of vitiated blood.
[The remedy consists of: māṇa, mārga, amṛtā, vāsā, sthirā, citraka, and rock salt.
One karṣa each of nāgara, tālagaṇḍa, and fresh trikaṭu, along with one karṣa each of viḍalavaṇa, sauvarcala, kṣāra, and pippalī—
all these should be powdered together and cooked in one āḍhaka of cow’s urine.
When it has become thick, one should form pills by adding three *palas* of honey.

This formulation, named Parikara, cures enlargement of the liver and spleen, abdominal dropsy, abdominal tumors, hemorrhoids, and malabsorption syndrome; it is a supreme stimulant for the digestive fire.
Urine or water infused with the powder of *rohitaka* and *abhayā*, when drunk, cures all types of abdominal enlargements, splenic disorders, urinary diseases, hemorrhoids, worms,
and abdominal tumors. Pippalī, ginger, and dantī in equal parts, with twice the amount of abhayā—
This powder, when drunk with warm water along with half a part of viḍa salt, indeed destroys splenic enlargement.
One should increase the dose by ten pippalīs daily for ten days in conjunction with milk, and then decrease it again in the same manner.
One should eat a *yaṣṭika* stick after each meal has been digested, along with milk and ghee.
This application of one thousand *pippalī*s is a rejuvenative (*rasāyana*).
Ten *pippalī*s per dose is considered best; six is declared to be middling.
The regimen that extends up to three *pippalī*s is considered the inferior one.
[However,] the elixir (*rasāyana*) of *pippalī* is nourishing, aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, a destroyer of splenic enlargement, stabilizing for youth, and promotes intelligence.

The *vardhamānaka* (gradually increasing dose) consisting of five *pippalī*s is also observed; these should be ground and drunk by those of strong constitution, boiled by those of medium strength, and cooled for those of weak strength, according to the specific bodily humors and diseases. (23)
Having ground the roots of pippalī and citraka, one should properly cook ghee with four times as much milk; this removes enlargement of the liver and spleen (yakṛt-plīhodara).
Ghee mixed with a paste of pippalī and four times as much milk [is likewise effective].
One should drink [this], which is supreme for removing diseases of the spleen, weak digestion, and liver disorders.
(25) One should cook one prastha of ghee in a decoction of one tulā of citraka, adding twice as much āraṇāla and four times as much whey (dadhi-maṇḍa). (26)
With the five pungents (pañcakolaka), the four salts (tālīsa-kṣāra), combined with salt,

two types of cumin (dvijīraka), and the two types of turmeric (niśā-yugma), one should add black pepper (marica) therein. [This cures] splenic disorders, abdominal tumors, enlargement of the abdomen, flatulence, anemia, loss of appetite, and fever.
When drunk, it destroys pain in the bladder, heart, flanks, hips, and thighs, as well as upward-moving wind (udāvarta) and chronic rhinitis (pīnasa).
It is a destroyer of hemorrhoids, a reducer of swelling, and an inflamer of the digestive fire; it also promotes strength and complexion, and it subdues morbid consumption (bhasmaka).
One should prepare a decoction using twenty-five palas of the best rohitaka bark, combined with two prasthas of kola;
this decoction should be mixed with one pala each of the five pungent spices (pañcakola) and an equal amount of all these ingredients combined.
One should cook one prastha of ghee with the ground bark of *rohitaka*.

When administered promptly, this quickly pacifies enlargement of the spleen (*plīhābhivṛddhi*), as well as abdominal tumors (*gulma*), fever, dyspnea, worms, anemia (*pāṇḍutva*), and jaundice (*kāmalā*).
One should grind one hundred palas of *rohitaka* and one *āḍhaka* of *badara* fruit;
having boiled these in one *droṇa* of water until reduced to one-fourth,
one should add one *prastha* of ghee and four times as much goat’s milk.
Into that [mixture], one should add all these following pastes (kalka), each measured by a single akṣa:
the three pungents (vyoṣa), the three fruits (phalatrika), asafoetida (hiṅgu), yamānī, tumburu, biḍa salt, cumin (ajājī), black salt (kṛṣṇalavaṇa), pomegranate (dāḍima), and devadāru. || 34–35 ||
Punarnavā, viśālā, yavakṣāra, pauṣkara, viḍaṅga, citraka, hapuṣā, cavikā, and vacā— with these,
one should cook ghee and store it in a sturdy vessel.
One should administer a dose of three palas, having regard for the disease and the patient's strength.
Then, one should feed the patient with meat broth, vegetable soup, or milk.
Once that ghee has been consumed, it destroys these many diseases.
It pacifies enlargement of the liver and spleen, as well as splenic pain, liver disease,
abdominal pain, cardiac pain, pain in the flanks,
loss of appetite, obstructive colic, and jaundice accompanied by icterus.
It pacifies vomiting and diarrhea, destroys drowsiness and fever, and is known as Mahārohitaka; it is especially effective in destroying splenic disorders. (40) Chapter 38.
Water boiled with ginger, punarnavā, castor root, and the five roots (pañcamūla) is recommended for edema caused by vāta, both as a drink and as an ingredient in food;
likewise, daśamūla is beneficial in every respect, especially in cases of vāta.
In swelling caused by pitta, one who subsists on milk should drink a decoction of trivṛt, guḍūcī,
and triphalā mixed with cow’s urine.
Then, one akṣa-measure of the powder of the three fruits (triphalā) [should be taken].
Abhayā, dāru, madhuka, tiktā, dantī, pippalī, paṭola, candana, dārvī, trāyamāṇā, and indravāruṇī—[these are the ingredients]. 3.

The decoction of these, mixed with ghee, cures swelling, fever, burning sensations, erysipelas, thirst, heat, and disorders of the *sannipāta* type caused by poisons; furthermore, one should perform massages and other treatments with cold- potency substances and ice water.
A paste of punarnavā, viśva, trivṛt, guḍūcī, sampāka, pathyā, and amaradāru,
combined with mahiṣākṣa, [is used] for swelling caused by kapha.
Or one should drink their urine or water in the same manner.
In the case of phlegm (kapha), however, there should be an external application of black pepper, sand, old oil-cake, śigru bark, and hemp.
Sprinkling with water decocted with *kulattha*, ginger, and cow urine,
as well as anointing with *caṇḍā* and *aguru*;
[and using] *ajājī*, *pāṭhā*, *ghana*, and the five *kolas*.
The roots of vyāghrī, rajanī, bhūnimba, and mahauṣadha, when drunk with pleasant water, destroy swelling caused by the three doṣas, even if it is chronic or advanced.
A decoction of punarnavā, nimba, paṭola,
śuṇṭhī, tiktā, amṛtā, dāru, and abhayā [is used for] swelling of the entire body, abdominal enlargement, cough, and colic.
It destroys asthma accompanied by anemia. 8.
The juice of fresh ginger, drunk mixed with old jaggery by those who consume goat's milk, quickly removes all types of swelling. 9.
Guggulu taken with a decoction of punarnavā, dāru, and śuṇṭhī, or with cow’s urine alone, or even with a decoction of daśamūla, destroys swelling.
Purified bilva leaf juice is a drying agent for swelling caused by the three doṣas.
One should also administer it in cases of vit-saṅga, durnāman, and kāmalā.
The powder of jaggery, pippalī, and śuṇṭhī destroys swelling,
pacifies indigestion caused by undigested matter (āma), relieves colic, and cleanses the bladder.

For those suffering from edema, one should consume long pepper (pippalī) with urine, or with milk, or equal parts of myrobalan (abhayā) with jaggery, or ginger (viśva), or jaggery with fresh ginger (guḍārdraka),
or jaggery with dry ginger (guḍanāgara). || 13 ||
A person should eat either jaggery with long pepper or jaggery with long pepper, increasing by one karṣa at a time until it reaches a measure of three palas, for a fortnight or even a month. (14)
It cures edema, catarrh, diseases of the throat and mouth, as well as dyspnea, cough, anorexia, chronic rhinitis,
chronic fever, hemorrhoids, and disorders of the digestive tract.
Likewise, it destroys other diseases of kapha and vāta.
A paste made from sthalapadma, stirred with milk and administered as a drink, cures splenic disorders and conquers swelling of the entire body or of a single limb. 15–16.
A paste of *dāru*, *guggulu*, and *śuṇṭhī* taken with urine conquers swelling; or a paste of *varṣābhū* and *śṛṅgavera* conquers all types of swelling.
Having prepared a decoction of *siṃhāsya*, *amṛta*, and *bhaṇḍākī*, one should take it with honey.
Having drunk this, a person may conquer swelling, dyspnea, cough, vomiting, and fever.
Having consumed a paste of *bhūnimba* and *viśva*, a decoction of *punarnavā* should be drunk;
it certainly and quickly removes swelling affecting all parts of the body in men.

The ash of *kokilākṣa* taken with urine or water cures swelling; likewise, milk boiled with *dāru*, *varṣābhū*, and *nāgara* removes swelling. Alternatively, one should drink milk prepared with *citraka*, *vyoṣa*, *trivṛt*, and *dāru*.
Juices, gruels, milks, and soups prepared with punarnavā, mūlaka, kapittha, dāru, chinnodbhavā, and the roots of citraka [are beneficial].
In cases of swelling, [decoctions] containing the ten roots (daśamūla) should be administered.
There should be the two types of alkali (kṣāra), the four salts, iron filings (ayo-rajas), the three pungents (vyoṣa), and the three fruits (phalatrika).
Long pepper root, viḍaṅga pith, mustā, ajamodā, amaradāru, bilva, kaliṅgaka, citraka root, and pāṭhā— [these are the ingredients]. || 22 ||
One karṣa each of yaṣṭyāhvaya, ativiṣā, and palāśa, along with asafoetida, and likewise one droṇa of dried radish and ginger powder. (23)
That ash should be prepared with water;
having stirred it until it becomes thick and no longer burns, one should then take a dose the size of a jujube fruit from that solidified mass.
Having prepared it according to the prescribed method until it is thoroughly dried, one should employ it [as a medicinal paste] for the treatment of splenic enlargement,
vitiligo, chlorosis, hemorrhoids, anemia, anorexia, edema, and consumption.
It dispels cholera, abdominal tumors, artificial poisons, urinary stones, as well as asthma, cough, and skin diseases.
[25] So too do sauvarcala, saindhava, biḍa, and audbhida salts.
In this [preparation], there should be four parts of salt and eight parts of water;
[along with] punarnavā, citraka, devadāru,
the five pungents (pañcoṣaṇa), alkali (kṣāra), and harītakī.
Ghee cooked with the paste [of drugs] in a decoction of the ten roots (daśamūla) is the best for destroying swelling.
Ghee prepared with the decoction and paste of punarnavā likewise removes swelling.

Ghee boiled with the paste of viśvaupadha in a decoction of daśamūla cures swelling, malabsorption syndrome (grahaṇī), and anemia (pāṇḍu). [Likewise, ghee prepared with] citraka, dhānyaka, yamānī, and pāṭhā [is effective].
Long pepper, the three pungents (ginger, black pepper, and long pepper), vetasāmla, the fruit of bilva, pomegranate, barley-ash,
long pepper root, and also chavya. || 29 ||
Having ground [the ingredients] into portions the size of an akṣa and boiled them with one āḍhaka of water, one should then consume one prastha of ghee; this cures hemorrhoids,
abdominal tumors, edema, and dysuria.
It extinguishes fire and makes it blaze. One should digest ghee with the decoction of *pañcakola* and *kulattha*;
likewise, ghee prepared with a paste of *punarnavā* destroys swelling.
When milk placed in a jar smeared with a paste of *citraka* turns into curd, one should churn it thoroughly and extract the resulting ghee;
this, along with a paste of *citraka* root, [is used].
This foremost preparation, perfected with buttermilk, destroys swelling; it cures hemorrhoids, diarrhea, wind-disorders, abdominal tumors, and urinary disorders,
and it increases strength.
One should cook one *prastha* of ghee with the decoction and paste of *māṇaka*; it dispels swelling caused by a single *doṣa*, by two *doṣas*, or by all three *doṣas*.
Eight *palas* of *sthalapadma* leaves and four *palas* of *tryūṣaṇa* [should be used].
One should cook one *prastha* of ghee with these [drugs], adding four times as much milk;
this quickly cures the five types of cough as well as even the most difficult edema. [The drugs are: *śaileya*, *kuṣṭha*, *aguru*, *dāru*, and *kauntī*.
With cinnamon, lotus stalks, kailāba, palāśa, and musta;
with priyaṅgu, sthauṇeyaka, hema, māṃsī, tālīsa, patra, plava, patra, and dhānya. || 36 ||

In cases accompanied by Vata, they recommend an oil prepared with śrīveṣṭaka, dhyāmaka, and pippalī, or alternatively with pṛkkā and nakhī, according to availability, for external application over the affected limbs.
An ointment made even from well-ground [powders] is effective.
Oil cooked with dried radish, varṣābhū, dāru, rāsnā, and mahauṣadha, when used for massage, overcomes swelling accompanied by pain.
One should cook one *āḍhaka* of the decoction of punarnavā, amṛtā, dāru, and the ten roots, along with one *prastha* of fresh ginger juice and one *tulā* of jaggery.
When this is prepared, one should add one *karṣa* each of the three pungents (vyoṣa), cavya, elā, and tvak.
One should add a *kuḍava* of honey to these when they have become cool and lick the preparation;
this electuary named *paunarnava* destroys swelling and colic, removes dyspnea, cough, and loss of appetite, and increases strength, complexion, and digestive fire. (40–41)

One should boil one hundred *pathyā* fruits in a *kaṃsa* (four āḍhakas) of the decoction of the ten roots (*daśamūla*). When it has thickened, one should add one *tulā* of jaggery (*guḍa*), four *palas* each of the three pungents (*vyoṣa*) and alkali (*kṣāra*), and one part of gold (*suvarṇa*) of the three aromatics (*trisugandha*). Once it has cooled, half a *prastha* of honey should be added.

The *daśamūlī-harītakī* formulation destroys even the most severe swellings, as well as fevers, anorexia, abdominal tumors, hemorrhoids, urinary disorders, anemia, and diseases of the abdomen. Of the three aromatics (*trisugandha*), one *karṣa* each should be taken. (43–44)
This *kaṃsaharītakī* is taught differently in the *Caraka-saṃhitā*;
its equivalence in measure is described there as well. One should boil [the drugs] in a decoction of the two sets of five roots (*pañcamūla*).

One hundred *abhayā* fruits and sugar should be added to a well-prepared medicinal electuary (*lehya*) in a bronze vessel; once it has been properly cooked, the powder of *vyoṣa*, the three aromatics (*trisaugandhya*), and *uśīra* should be mixed in when it has reached the desired consistency. || 46 ||
Having consumed half a *prastha* of well-cooled honey along with a small amount of powdered barley-sugar (*yāvaśūka*) and one *abhayā*, one should then take the electuary.
It destroys swelling and severe edema,
as well as cough, fever, anorexia, urinary disorders, abdominal tumors,
splenic enlargement, and anemia arising from the three doṣas.
[It cures] emaciation, āmavāta, blood disorders, acidity, pitta, discoloration, and defects of the urine, flatus, and semen.
48. No further commentary has been provided here.
The explanation is the same as before regarding that which is auspicious.
An ointment made of sesame, milk, honey, and fresh butter destroys eruptions and swelling.
Alternatively, with the earth from the foot of that tree or with *śāla* leaves, swelling caused by poison will subside before long;
in cases of swelling due to poison, the treatment prescribed for poison is recommended.

Village-grown grains, marshy meat, salt, dried vegetables, fresh grain, preparations of molasses, flour-based foods, curd, rice-and-pulse porridge, slimy substances, wine, sour items, parched grain, dried meat, eating in equal proportions [of incompatible foods], as well as heavy, unwholesome, and burning-to-the-throat food.
One suffering from swelling should avoid sexual intercourse during the night and while dreaming.
Adhikāra 39:
A person should drink either guggulu or *rubu* oil with cow's urine.
It quickly destroys an increase of Vāta that has persisted for a long time. Alternatively, one should drink castor oil with milk for a month, or likewise the oil of *punarnavā*, or *nārāyaṇa* oil.
In cases of urinary disorders or groin pain, oil should be drunk with water decocted with the ten roots;
